_about: Legal words explained two ways. 'teen' = our plain version, 'official' = the formal meaning. 'match' = the exact words to look for (longest first is handled by the code). Edit freely; information only, not legal advice.

terms.teen: Out-of-court settlement: a private referee decides, not a judge.
terms.official: A way of settling a dispute outside the courts: the parties agree that one or more neutral arbitrators will hear the case and make a decision (an award) that is usually binding and can be challenged only on limited grounds.

terms.teen: Lots of people suing a company together, as one team.
terms.official: A lawsuit brought by one or more people on behalf of a larger group who have similar claims against the same defendant.

terms.teen: If someone sues them because of you, you pay.
terms.official: To compensate or protect another party against loss, damage or legal liability arising from specified events or conduct.

terms.teen: Permission to use your stuff. You still own it.
terms.official: Legal permission granted by the owner of rights (such as copyright) allowing another party to use the protected material within stated limits, without transferring ownership.

terms.teen: They don't pay you for using it.
terms.official: Permission to use material without paying royalties or ongoing fees to the rights holder.

terms.teen: They can pass the permission on to other companies.
terms.official: A licence term allowing the licensee to grant some or all of its licensed rights to third parties.

terms.teen: They can hand the permission to someone else.
terms.official: Capable of being assigned or conveyed to another party.

terms.teen: New stuff made from your stuff, like edits or remixes.
terms.official: A new work based on one or more existing works, such as a translation, adaptation or modification.

terms.teen: Forever. No end date.
terms.official: Lasting indefinitely, without a fixed end date.

terms.teen: You can't take it back later.
terms.official: Cannot be cancelled or withdrawn once granted.

terms.teen: Another company or person, not you and not the app.
terms.official: A person or organisation that is not one of the main parties to an agreement.

terms.teen: Info that shows who you are: name, number, face, location.
terms.official: Information relating to an identified or identifiable individual. India's DPDP Act, 2023 defines it as any data about an individual who is identifiable by or in relation to such data.

terms.teen: Saying yes, knowing what you're saying yes to.
terms.official: Agreement given voluntarily by a person who understands what they are agreeing to. Under India's DPDP Act, 2023 it must be free, specific, informed, unconditional and unambiguous, given by a clear affirmative action.

terms.teen: Your parent has to say OK first.
terms.official: Permission given by a parent or lawful guardian on behalf of a minor. Under India's DPDP Act, 2023, verifiable consent of a parent is required before a child's (under 18) personal data is processed.

terms.teen: India's 2023 law that protects your personal data.
terms.official: The Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023: India's law on processing digital personal data, setting rules on consent, children's data and the rights of individuals (called Data Principals).

terms.teen: Anyone under 18 in India.
terms.official: A person below the age of majority; in India, generally under 18 years.

terms.teen: Which country's laws apply, and where you'd go to court.
terms.official: Governing law is the legal system chosen to interpret a contract; jurisdiction is the authority of a particular court to hear and decide a case.

terms.teen: Who pays if something goes wrong.
terms.official: Legal responsibility for one's acts or omissions. A limitation of liability clause restricts the amount or types of damages a party can be required to pay.

terms.teen: Giving up a right you normally have.
terms.official: The voluntary giving up of a known legal right or claim.

terms.teen: End it, like closing your account.
terms.official: To bring a contract or relationship to an end, as permitted by its terms.

terms.teen: Tiny files that help sites remember and track you.
terms.official: Small data files stored on a user's device by a website, used to remember information such as logins, preferences or browsing activity.

terms.teen: Info about your stuff: when, where and to whom.
terms.official: Data that describes other data, such as the time, location, sender or file details of a message or photo.

terms.teen: Ads picked for you from what you watch and like.
terms.official: Advertising selected for an individual based on data about their behaviour, interests or characteristics.

terms.teen: Ads that look like normal posts.
terms.official: Content paid for by an advertiser and presented on a platform, often in a format similar to regular content.

terms.teen: It keeps charging you until you cancel.
terms.official: A contract term under which a subscription continues for a new period, and is billed, unless cancelled before the renewal date.

terms.teen: How long they keep your info.
terms.official: The period for which an organisation stores data, and its rules for keeping and deleting it.

terms.teen: Body data: your face, fingerprint or voice.
terms.official: Data from physical or behavioural characteristics used to identify a person, such as fingerprints, facial geometry or voiceprints.

terms.teen: Saying 'no thanks' to something that's on by default.
terms.official: Choosing not to take part in a practice, such as data sharing, that applies by default unless the user declines.

terms.teen: Scrambling data so only the right people can read it.
terms.official: Converting information into a code to prevent unauthorised access.
